questions.q: Before reading something longer than a tweet, what should you ask yourself?
a: Why am I reading this, and why do I need its information?
How many pages does this have and how fast can I finish?
Who recommended this and will they quiz me?
Is this the newest title on the subject?
questions.why: Lesson 1 gives two questions that help you read less of what you don't need.

questions.q: What is the main idea of lesson 1 on reading more?
a: Read less of what you don't need to
Read everything as fast as possible
Finish every book you start
Reread important pages three times
questions.why: The lesson says the easiest way to read more is to skip unneeded material.

questions.q: What does a preview involve, according to lesson 2?
a: Scanning the title, foreword, back flap and index, then headings
Reading the last chapter in full first
Listening to an audio version at high speed
Asking a friend to summarize the book
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes previewing the front matter, index, headings and opening sentences.

questions.q: Roughly how much of a text's information can a preview give you?
a: Up to 40 percent
About 5 percent
Nearly 100 percent
Around 75 percent
questions.why: The summary says previewing can reveal up to 40% of the information.

questions.q: Why does the summary say to focus on keywords?
a: They carry a sentence's meaning, so you can read more fluently
They let you skip every other paragraph
They replace the need to preview
They make fiction easier to skim
questions.why: Lesson 3 says following key words lets your eyes move more smoothly.
